text: In propositional resolution, deriving the *empty clause* □ from a set of clauses Γ shows that:
choices: every clause in Γ is a single literal
Γ is satisfiable, and □ names a satisfying assignment
Γ is unsatisfiable (resolution refutation is complete)
explanation: Resolution is refutation-complete: the empty clause is derivable from Γ iff Γ is unsatisfiable. The empty clause represents a contradiction — not a tautology (option 1) or a satisfying assignment (option 3) — and has nothing to do with clauses being single literals (option 2).
